title: CM-Transform: Co-Activation Permuted Block Sparsity and Cache-Line Aligned Execution for Transformer Inference on Commodity Hardware
description:
Reference implementation, evaluation harness and result snapshots for the CM-Transform study. The work asks a narrow question: feed-forward blocks in modern SwiGLU/GELU transformers carry no exact-zero structure, so any compute saving must come from deciding which 32-lane blocks are worth evaluating, and from making that decision cheap enough to survive contact with real memory traffic.

What the repository contains: the reference forward pass of the five checkpoints used (Qwen3-0.6B, Qwen3.5-0.8B, Qwen3.5-4B-IQ4_NL, whisper-base, SmolVLM2-256M-Video-Instruct) written as plain weight dictionaries, functionally isomorphic 32-lane permutations of the FFN intermediate dimension, per-layer adaptive energy thresholds with norm-preserving rescaling, block-major IQ4_NL repacking inside 64-byte cache lines, CUDA / AVX-512 / scalar kernels, every benchmark driver behind the paper, the raw result JSONs, and the compiled manuscript.

Headline measurements on one consumer GPU (RTX 5070 Laptop, 8 GB) and one Zen 5 CPU: a functionally isomorphic permutation reproduces the dense forward pass to 1e-7; at a matched 20% skip budget on Qwen3.5-0.8B the WikiText-2 perplexity cost is +1.68 (6.2%) against +2.41 for CATS-Block, +2.30 for TEAL-Block and +13.17 for Wanda-style block pruning; block-major IQ4_NL gives 1.74x at 0% skip and 3.84-5.67x at 20-80% skip on a cold single layer; the whisper encoder keeps WER 6.21% with 20% of blocks removed (6.08% dense). The paper also reports the byte ceilings that bound decode-time numbers, the dispatch-cost boundary where skipping loses to dense execution, and the measurements where skipping loses.

Reproduction: pip install -r requirements.txt, python3 scripts/fetch_models.py (third-party checkpoints, not redistributed; pinned by size and SHA-256 in MODELS.md), then bash scripts/verify.sh (dependency check, checkpoint digests, 77 tests, reference-vs-official forward comparison, artefact digests). Without the checkpoints the suite still runs 33 checks and skips the model-dependent modules. Result files carry their seed (1234) and the exact checkpoint digest they were produced from.

The manuscript is paper2_bundle/CM_Transform_Paper2_Final.pdf (Typst source alongside it, 20 pages, 45 tables, 6 figures). It was typeset while the code lived at github.com/no-nova/CM-CNN, so its title-page link names that path; this repository is the canonical home of the code, results and manuscript.

notes: Third-party checkpoints (Qwen3-0.6B, Qwen3.5-0.8B, Qwen3.5-4B-IQ4_NL, whisper-base, SmolVLM2-256M-Video-Instruct) and the LibriSpeech audio are not redistributed: they remain under their own licences. MODELS.md records the source repository, file name, byte size and SHA-256 of each weight file, and scripts/fetch_models.py re-verifies them. The real-video frames and the result table of the companion CM-CNN study are likewise absent; only the video-conditioned drivers need them and they say so explicitly. Compiled kernels (*.so, results/build/) and cached tensors (*.pt) are build products and are regenerated by the scripts in experiments/cm-transformer/. Evaluation splits in data/benchmarks/ keep the licences of their source datasets: WikiText-2 CC BY-SA 3.0, ARC CC BY-SA 4.0, BoolQ CC BY-SA 3.0, PIQA AFL-3.0, GSM8K MIT, POPE BSD-3-Clause.
